report.summary: One review-recommended drift finding: GET /profile now exposes tax ID and date of birth that are not covered by a modeled information asset.

findings.title: New tax ID and date-of-birth response data is not classified

model_excerpt.quote: Usernames and password hashes in the users table

evidence.note: Adds TaxID as the JSON field tax_id in the profile API response type.
Adds DateOfBirth as the JSON field date_of_birth in the profile API response type.
Populates the newly exposed tax ID from the signed-in user's record.
Populates the newly exposed date of birth from the signed-in user's record.

relevance.justification: The change directly exposes two sensitive personal-data fields through GET /profile, while the only modeled information asset is limited to usernames and password hashes.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl in threat model "login service": add an information_asset block for profile personal data returned by GET /profile, explicitly covering email, tax ID, and date of birth with an appropriate sensitive classification. This is motivated by internal/httpapi/user.go:11-12 and :23-24, which add tax_id and date_of_birth to the profile response; the existing "user credentials" asset at app.tm.hcl:7 only covers usernames and password hashes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a classified information asset for profile personal data covering email, tax ID, and date of birth returned by GET /profile.
